title: International Guides Bureau - Applications For Passports Received From Russian Emigrants

REPORT

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 7580
Branch: Special
Date February 22nd 38

Subject International Guides Bureau - applications for passports received
from Russian emigrants.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

（左侧手写批注：Further inquiries being made by S.I. / Gls P.T. / 2/2. / 23 v / F.A. to D cks Sr.)

On February 21, 1938 information was received to the effect that Russian emigrants in Shanghai who wish to proceed to foreign countries may obtain the necessary passports through the medium of the International Guides Bureau, 180 Nanking Road.

Upon visiting the said Bureau for the purpose of verification of the above information the undersigned was referred to a Chinese who gave his name as Mr. S.Y. Kiang. He stated that any Russian emigrant wishing to apply for a passport to enable him to proceed to foreign countries may do so at the International Guides Bureau who, it would appear, act as agents of the Hongkong office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the National Government.

Applicants are requested to show their passports or certificates of registration, to fill in an application form ( specimen attached together with a translation), to furnish 4 copies of their photographs and to pay $ 25.00 fees. Passports are received from Hongkong after about three weeks from the date of application.

Mr. Kiang did not give the name and address of the issuing office, but stated that this arrangement was quite in order and that for all practical purposes it was sufficient to know that passports were issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

This seems to be the only way out of the situation created by the closure on February 2, 1938 of the Shanghai office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 6 Tifeng Road, as certificates issued to Russian emigrants by the local representative of Nansen Office are not recognized as passports by certain foreign consulates in Shanghai.

日期：1938年2月22日

事由：国际导游局——收到的俄国侨民护照申请。

呈报人：副督察普罗科菲耶夫（D.S.I. Prokofiev）。转呈人：督察克劳福德（C. Crawford D.I.）。

（左侧手写批注：副督察正在进一步查询 / Gls P.T. / 2/2. / 23 v / F.A. 致 D cks Sr.)

1938年2月21日，接获情报称，希望前往外国的在沪俄国侨民可通过南京路180号的“国际导游局”（International Guides Bureau）获取所需护照。

为核实上述信息，具名者走访了该局，被引见给一位自称姜先生（Mr. S.Y. Kiang）的华人。他表示，任何希望申请护照以便前往外国的俄国侨民均可向国际导游局提出申请；该局似乎是国民政府外交部香港办事处的代理机构。

申请人需出示护照或登记证，填写申请表（附样本及译文），提供四张照片，并缴纳25.00美元费用。护照通常在申请之日起约三周后从香港寄达。

姜先生未提供发证机关的名称和地址，但声称此安排完全合规，且就实际目的而言，只需知道护照由外交部签发即可。

这似乎是解决因1938年2月2日关闭的位于提篮桥路6号（Tifeng Road）的上海外交部办事处所造成的困境的唯一途径，因为南森办公室（Nansen Office）当地代表向俄国侨民签发的证书不被上海某些外国领事馆承认为护照。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 29, 1937

Sightseeing Bus Ride
For Tourists Planned

Something new for Shanghal-landers who stick close to their homes and offices, as well as for the myriads of tourists who visit the city, is a unique sightseeing bus shortly to be placed in service by the International Guides Bureau, of which Mrs. Hanne Burst is the manager. Members of the press were taken on a special inaugural trip of the new vehicle this morning, driving round Hongkew way, where, incidentally, everything seems quiet and peaceful.

One of the main features of the coach, which was designed and mounted on a Reo chasis by the Mark L. Moody Company, is its glass roof, through which Shanghai's bright lights, as well as the summer skies, can be glimpsed on the evening trips. To provide for the comfort of the passengers, 21 of whom can be carried at one time, in addition to the driver and a guide, a Philco radio has been installed, and the Hazelwood Co. plans to arrange for the stocking and serving of ice-cream in the bus. Both within and without, the "crystal bus," as the Bureau describes it, is finished in silver and apple-green, presenting a cool and restful appearance.

Every-day service is planned by the Bureau, who intend to have four trips a day, including weekends. The first daily trip will be from 9 to 12 in the morning, which is to be followed by an afternoon shopping excursion from 2 to 6 p.m., especially for tourists, who will be set down at various shopping centres and given half-an-hour or so to make their purchases. A slightly shorter trip is the evening one, from 6.30 to 8.30, and those visitors who wish to see Shanghai's famed night-life can do so on still another, from 9 p.m. to 2 a.m. Diverse points of interest will be visited on the general trips, and special ones can be arranged upon request of 18 or more persons. Bookings can be made at the Bureau or at leading hotels. These excursions commence at the Broadway Mansions, and the bus will stop at various hotels and other meeting-places en route, according to the day's schedule. All trips except the shortest, which is priced at $3 are $5 a seat.

Besides affording visitors and local residents alike an opportunity of "seeing Shanghai deluxe" in their new bus, the International Guides Bureau is sponsoring flights over Shanghai by planes of the Eurasia Aviation Corporation from 4 to 6 p.m. every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, and is also trying to establish a "social guide" system similar to that of other cities.

（批：July 29）

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年7月29日，星期四

为游客策划的
观光巴士之旅

对于那些足不出户、坚守办公室的上海居民，以及成千上万来访的游客来说，一件新鲜事是国际导游局即将投入运营的独特观光巴士，该局局长为汉娜·伯斯特（Hanne Burst）夫人。今天上午，新闻界人士受邀乘坐新车进行特别的 inaugural 之旅，绕行虹口地区，顺便一提，那里的一切似乎都宁静祥和。

这辆由 Mark L. Moody 公司设计并安装在 Reo 底盘上的长途客车的主要特点之一是其玻璃车顶，在晚间行程中可以透过它瞥见上海的璀璨灯火以及夏日天空。为了保障乘客的舒适，该车除司机和导游外可容纳21人，车内安装了 Philco 收音机，Hazelwood 公司计划安排在车上供应冰淇淋。无论内部还是外部，正如该局所描述的，“水晶巴士”均采用银色和苹果绿色装饰，呈现出凉爽宜人的外观。

该局计划每天提供服务，包括周末，每天四班。每日首班车时间为上午9点至12点，随后是下午2点至6点的购物短途旅行，专为游客设计，他们将在各个购物中心下车，并有半小时左右的时间购物。晚间行程稍短，从6:30到8:30，而那些希望领略上海著名夜生活的游客还可以参加另一班，从晚上9点到凌晨2点。常规行程将参观各个兴趣点，如有18人或以上的团体要求，可安排特别行程。预订可在该局或主要酒店进行。这些短途旅行从百老汇大厦（Broadway Mansions）出发，巴士将根据当天的时间表在沿途各家酒店和其他集合点停靠。除最短行程定价为3美元外，所有行程座位费均为5美元。

除了让游客和当地居民都有机会在新巴士中“豪华游览上海”外，国际导游局还赞助欧亚航空公司（Eurasia Aviation Corporation）的飞机每周一、三、五下午4点至6点飞越上海上空，并正试图建立类似于其他城市的“社交导游”制度。

（批注：7月29日）
